author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Provisional write tier: speculative items are fully recorded yet excluded from proof-bearing surfaces until explicitly promoted, and discardable without weakening any chain

Every write to a pm workspace is immediately permanent proof. That is the correct default for delivery work and the wrong default for exploration, and the record shows the project has never had a way to say "this is provisional". The draft status exists in the schema and has been written zero times across 40,856 history entries and 2,176 items, so the provisional tier is nominal rather than real - it has no declared semantics, no surface excludes it, and nothing promotes or discards it.

The gap binds hardest exactly where the product is heading. An episodic harness - training, evaluation, benchmarking, or sim-to-real - explores. It creates candidate items, tries orderings, records observations that turn out to be wrong, and then wants either to keep the branch or to leave no trace. Today it has two options and both are bad. It can write into the live workspace, in which case every discarded hypothesis is permanent proof indistinguishable from delivered work, and the relevance engine will keep scoring it. Or it can snapshot and restore the whole workspace, which pm-dkrmzv delivered, but whole-workspace rollback destroys every other agent's concurrent writes, so it is unusable on a shared tracker with thousands of agents.

What is missing is a per-item provisional tier that coexists with permanent work in one live workspace:

  a provisional item is fully readable and mutable by its own author or episode
  it is excluded by default from work selection, context assembly, changelog derivation, and every proof-bearing surface
  promotion is an explicit, recorded transition that makes it permanent from that point forward
  discard is an explicit, recorded transition that retires the item without leaving a gap in any verifiable chain

The last clause is the hard one and the reason this is a feature rather than a status default. Discarding must not weaken the integrity guarantee. The provisional entries themselves are real history and must stay verifiable; what changes is their standing, not their existence. That distinguishes discard from deletion and puts this in direct conversation with pm-h6wmtc, which owns erasure against an immutable record, and with pm-e3gn0z, which proves that retiring an id today leaves a stream that can be silently reused.

Boundaries. pm-pww8ax owns the ratchet that notices never-exercised capabilities and is where the zero-draft-writes measurement lives; it says the capability is unused, not what it should mean. pm-li2fj5 owns the episode specification and is the primary consumer, not the owner of item lifecycle semantics. pm-0mhspz owns custom statuses being orphaned from work selection when they carry no lifecycle role, which is the general shape; this is the specific provisional role that shape needs and the one built-in status that already exists to carry it.

The provisional role is declared in the lifecycle registry rather than inferred from a status name, so custom statuses can adopt the same role and the built-in draft status is simply the first member; Provisional items are excluded by default from pm next, pm context, changelog derivation, aggregate rollups, and every relevance-scored surface, and each exclusion is a declared property of the role rather than a per-command condition; An explicit opt-in flag includes provisional items on any read surface, with a bounded and declared cost, so an episode can see its own speculative work without changing any default; Promotion and discard are distinct recorded transitions with their own history operations, and the recorded op vocabulary declares them, satisfying the enumeration rule pm-0elqjj establishes; A discarded provisional item leaves every hash chain verifiable and its id permanently retired rather than reusable, asserted by a test that runs pm history --verify and an id-reuse probe after discard; Provisional writes are per-item and require no workspace-level snapshot, proven by a concurrency test in which one agent explores and discards while another agent's permanent writes to the same workspace are unaffected; An episode can declare that all of its writes default to provisional, so a harness does not have to mark each write, and the declaration is part of the portable episode specification

message: File the provisional write tier that episodic exploration needs and the draft status has never been given
